subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Concrete's Carbon Problem
description: A 60-second lesson on Concrete's Carbon Problem.

hook.text: If the cement industry were a country, only China and the US would emit more CO2.

buildup.text: Heating limestone releases CO2 chemically — not just from fuel. Even clean energy can't eliminate half the emissions.

discovery.text: Carbon capture can trap CO2 at the kiln. Some startups inject captured CO2 back into concrete, minerilizing it.

twist.text: Demand for concrete is rising, not falling. Africa and Asia need infrastructure for billions of people.

climax.text: Geopolymer cements use industrial waste instead of limestone. They cut emissions by up to 80%.

punchline.text: We can't stop using concrete. We must reinvent it.

quiz.question: Why can't clean energy alone solve cement's CO2 problem?
options: Cement kilns cannot operate on renewable electricity
Half the emissions come from a chemical reaction in limestone, not fuel
Transporting cement requires diesel trucks that can't be electrified
